title: Exclude matching terms from memory recall
rubric: The CLI exposes a repeatable --exclude TERM option and recall(...) accepts an exclude_terms keyword with identical validation and normalization.
Exclude terms are tokenized case-insensitively with the same [a-z0-9]+, lowercase, drop one-character tokens and STOPWORDS rules used for query terms, then de-duplicated in first-seen order.
Empty, stopword-only, or one-character-only exclude arguments fail through argparse with exit status 2, while the function API raises ValueError with the same diagnostic text.
A fact is excluded only when a normalized exclude token equals a token from name, tags, description, or body; substring matches and provenance/scope fields do not count.
Exclusion happens after project/provider/expiration eligibility but before corpus statistics, relevance scoring, the relevance gate, sorting, and budget capping.
Active JSON output reports exclude_terms and withheld_excluded, while inactive markdown and JSON output remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Markdown reports the exact excluded-count note only when active exclusion withholds at least one fact, including the no-survivor case.
Remaining recalled facts preserve their existing scope, provenance, trust warning, state, body, ordering, and budget/drop semantics.
